songs_to_prepare.title: Let It Go
songs_to_prepare.why: Elsa's own defining number — shows the soprano-to-belt transformation and the character's emotional release

songs_to_prepare.title: Defying Gravity
songs_to_prepare.why: The closest theatrical parallel — a misunderstood woman transforming her pain into freedom and power

songs_to_prepare.title: The Music of the Night
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — shows the isolated figure creating a world inside a fortress, dark and beautiful

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know the Truth
songs_to_prepare.why: A woman facing hard truths about her power and what it costs — dramatic soprano/mezzo belt

frozen/frozen-elsa.style_guidance: Elsa needs a soprano who can do legit lyric AND a full mezzo-style belt to at least F5. The emotional journey is as important as the range. She is isolated, powerful, and terrified in equal measure.
avoid: Sweet Disney princess voices without the belt — Elsa needs real power behind the warmth

songs_to_prepare.title: For the First Time in Forever
songs_to_prepare.why: Anna's opening — warm, comic mezzo-soprano, hopeful and slightly over-excited

songs_to_prepare.title: Part of Your World
songs_to_prepare.why: Disney yearning mezzo-soprano who wants MORE — same energy as Anna, similar warmth

songs_to_prepare.title: Gimme Gimme
songs_to_prepare.why: Enthusiastic, heart-on-sleeve mezzo — big feelings delivered at full speed

songs_to_prepare.title: Not for the Life of Me
songs_to_prepare.why: Sunny contemporary mezzo — optimism, speed, and genuine warmth

frozen/frozen-anna.style_guidance: Anna is all heart and no filter — mezzo-soprano who is warm, funny, physically committed, and emotionally transparent. She is the emotional opposite of Elsa.
avoid: Controlled, restrained material — Anna is about overflow, not elegance

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Loved You
songs_to_prepare.why: Romantic legit baritone/tenor — Hans sells the love story with total conviction

songs_to_prepare.title: Anthem
songs_to_prepare.why: A man with a hidden agenda delivering passionate conviction — the trick is he means everything

songs_to_prepare.title: This Nearly Was Mine
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — shows the baritone's romantic depth before the reveal

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The young man who went out into the world with a plan — and found it complicated

frozen/frozen-hans.style_guidance: Hans must be utterly believable as the perfect romantic until the twist — baritone/tenor who is charming, warm, and invested. The audience must not see it coming. Save the edge.
avoid: Obvious villainous material for the audition — Hans must sell the romance completely first

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: A young man who is more emotionally complex than his rough exterior suggests — self-aware baritone

songs_to_prepare.title: Anthem
songs_to_prepare.why: Passionate baritone who loves something deeply and won't apologise for it

songs_to_prepare.title: Sunrise, Sunset
songs_to_prepare.why: Warm baritone showing unexpected emotional depth beneath the gruff surface

frozen/frozen-kristoff.style_guidance: Kristoff is the reluctant romantic — baritone who projects gruffness and delivers warmth. He is defined by action over words, so let the song reveal what he won't say.
avoid: Smooth polished leading-man style — Kristoff is rough around every edge

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Character tenor who lives to delight — innocent, enthusiastic, physically expressive

songs_to_prepare.title: In Summer
songs_to_prepare.why: Olaf's own number — shows the innocent wonder and comedic sincerity the role requires

songs_to_prepare.title: You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown
songs_to_prepare.from: You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown
songs_to_prepare.why: Pure-hearted character who finds joy in everything — character tenor with warm innocence

frozen/frozen-olaf.style_guidance: Olaf is wonder and warmth in snowman form — character tenor voice, physical comedy, and absolute genuine innocence. He is never sarcastic; every word is sincere.
avoid: Knowing or world-weary material — Olaf does not understand cynicism

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Only Had a Brain
songs_to_prepare.why: Physical character performance — movement-based role requiring strong physicality and mime skill

frozen/frozen-sven.style_guidance: Sven is a non-singing physical role — cast entirely on movement, mime, and puppy energy. Show physical work and character commitment rather than vocal pieces.
avoid: Trying to show a singing voice — this role is physical theatre first and last

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am the Very Model
songs_to_prepare.why: Self-important puffed-up character tenor — pompous, ridiculous, completely convinced of his own importance

songs_to_prepare.title: Sit Down, John
songs_to_prepare.why: Character who commands respect he has not earned — exasperated authority figure with comic pomposity

frozen/frozen-weselton.style_guidance: Weselton is the petty, preening political villain — character/character tenor with maximum comic pomposity. Physical comedy essential. Much funnier than he is dangerous.
avoid: Genuine menace — Weselton is comic relief, not a real threat

songs_to_prepare.title: Sunrise, Sunset
songs_to_prepare.why: Ancient, warm, paternal bass-baritone — the elder who knows more than he can say

songs_to_prepare.title: Make Them Hear You
songs_to_prepare.why: Deep, resonant character bass-baritone with gravitas and settled conviction

frozen/frozen-pabbie.style_guidance: Pabbie is ancient wisdom — low bass-baritone with gentleness and depth. Settles the audience with calm authority. Secondary role.
avoid: Young or aggressive material — Pabbie is primordial gentleness

songs_to_prepare.title: It's Today
songs_to_prepare.why: Warm, gregarious, overwhelming character baritone who is delighted by everything including you

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Character who makes every transaction into a theatrical event

frozen/frozen-oaken.style_guidance: Oaken is cheerfully enormous — big voice, big personality, big family, big sauna. Character baritone with maximum warmth and zero social radar.
avoid: Restrained material — Oaken does everything at full volume with complete enthusiasm

songs_to_prepare.title: Castle on a Cloud
songs_to_prepare.why: A frightened child dreaming of safety and warmth — pure treble with emotional vulnerability

songs_to_prepare.title: In My Own Little Corner
songs_to_prepare.why: The child who retreats into imagination from a world that doesn't understand her

frozen/frozen-young-elsa.style_guidance: Young Elsa carries enormous fear in a small voice — clear treble with genuine emotional fragility. The opening scenes land on this actress.
avoid: Powerful or adult material — Young Elsa is a frightened little girl, not a star

songs_to_prepare.title: Tomorrow
songs_to_prepare.why: The irrepressibly optimistic child — Young Anna condensed into three minutes

songs_to_prepare.title: Do Re Mi
songs_to_prepare.why: Pure childhood energy with a bright, clean treble — fun and absolutely zero filter

frozen/frozen-young-anna.style_guidance: Young Anna is pure sunshine and chaos — bright, warm child voice with comedian instincts. She bounces off walls including Elsa.
avoid: Quiet or introspective material — Young Anna has one gear: enthusiastic

songs_to_prepare.title: Gauntlet (Popular)
songs_to_prepare.why: Strong ensemble with character specificity — each Arendellian has a story

songs_to_prepare.title: Any Dream Will Do
songs_to_prepare.from: Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat
songs_to_prepare.why: Warm, versatile ensemble voice with lyric quality — Disney-adjacent style

frozen/frozen-ensemble-townspeople.style_guidance: Arendelle townspeople — warm, lyric ensemble sound with the ability to convey both celebration and fear. Frozen is a big-emotion show requiring committed ensemble work.
avoid: Pop-only approach — Frozen's ensemble writing is predominantly lyric/legit

songs_to_prepare.title: Be Our Guest
songs_to_prepare.why: Ensemble magic creatures — committed physicality, character work, and ensemble singing

frozen/frozen-ensemble-hidden-folk.style_guidance: Troll folk require strong physicality and character specificity — they are ancient, earthy, and lovingly meddlesome. Ensemble work with physical character transformation.
avoid: Realistic human physicality — trolls move and sing differently from humans

songs_to_prepare.title: Defying Gravity
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano/alto ensemble with power behind lyricism — shows the choral voice Frozen requires

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am the Very Model
songs_to_prepare.why: Demonstrates strong soprano/alto ensemble blend and musical precision

frozen/frozen-ensemble-snow-chorus.style_guidance: Snow Chorus is the ethereal choral body of the show — soprano/alto voices that blend beautifully, with the ability to convey both wonder and danger through pure tone.
avoid: Heavy belt for this ensemble — Snow Chorus is primarily lyric/legit in quality

songs_to_prepare.title: Out There
songs_to_prepare.why: Quasimodo's defining number — a soaring tenor cry for freedom from someone who has never had it

songs_to_prepare.title: The Music of the Night
songs_to_prepare.why: Another isolated, physically marked man believing in the world's beauty — tenor with ache

songs_to_prepare.title: Being Good Isn't Good Enough
songs_to_prepare.why: Earnest tenor who has done everything right and still gets no recognition — Quasimodo's frustration

songs_to_prepare.title: Anthem
songs_to_prepare.why: Passionate tenor/high baritone claiming identity against an indifferent world — climactic power

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-quasim.style_guidance: Quasimodo needs a high tenor with emotional rawness — out there to A4 is mandatory. The role requires genuine vulnerability and yearning, not just power. The bell tower is loneliness made musical.
avoid: Playing the disability — Quasimodo's spirit soars, the physical restriction is context, not character

songs_to_prepare.title: Hellfire
songs_to_prepare.why: Frollo's terrifying soliloquy — bass-baritone who turns religious conviction into obsessive desire

songs_to_prepare.title: Stars
songs_to_prepare.why: The great antagonist bass-baritone who believes God is on his side — righteous and terrifying

songs_to_prepare.title: The Music of the Night
songs_to_prepare.why: Obsessive, controlling baritone who believes his darkness is beautiful — the same shadow energy

songs_to_prepare.title: Epiphany
songs_to_prepare.why: The moment a controlled man's darkness fully escapes — chilling bass-baritone of absolute conviction

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-frollo.style_guidance: Frollo is one of the great musical theatre villains — a bass-baritone whose terror comes from total sincerity. He is not evil to himself. He believes in his righteousness absolutely.
avoid: Broad pantomime villain energy — Frollo's menace comes from cold conviction, not twirling

songs_to_prepare.title: God Help the Outcasts
songs_to_prepare.why: Esmeralda's own prayer — mezzo-soprano with spiritual conviction and raw emotional truth

songs_to_prepare.title: Don't Rain on My Parade
songs_to_prepare.why: Unstoppable mezzo-soprano force — the woman who will not be contained or defined by others

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know the Truth
songs_to_prepare.why: Dramatic mezzo belt — a woman with compassion and strength facing an unjust world

songs_to_prepare.title: Somewhere
songs_to_prepare.why: The yearning for a world without persecution — Esmeralda's deepest wish in musical form

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-esmera.style_guidance: Esmeralda is compassion and defiance in equal parts — mezzo-soprano who can deliver a folk-inflected belt and a spiritual legit line. She believes in justice with every note.
avoid: Passive, gentle material — Esmeralda is fierce, not soft, even in her most vulnerable moments

songs_to_prepare.title: The Impossible Dream
songs_to_prepare.why: The soldier becoming a man of conscience — baritone/tenor who discovers honour mid-story

songs_to_prepare.title: Anthem
songs_to_prepare.why: A man who has served institutions and now serves something higher — passionate, climactic baritone

songs_to_prepare.title: Being Alive
songs_to_prepare.why: A man confronting what truly matters — Phoebus's arc is about awakening to real love and justice

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-phoebu.style_guidance: Phoebus begins as a pragmatist and becomes a hero — baritone/tenor with inherent warmth and the capacity for moral growth. He needs to be believably both a soldier and a romantic.
avoid: Cold, calculating material — Phoebus's conversion to conscience must feel genuine

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: The theatrical MC who sets the tone for the whole show — showman energy, control of the audience

songs_to_prepare.title: Not While I'm Around
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows tenor baritone with complex moral ambiguity — Clopin protects his people but by any means

songs_to_prepare.title: Willkommen
songs_to_prepare.why: The great theatrical host who welcomes you to a world that may or may not be safe — exactly Clopin

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-clopin.style_guidance: Clopin is the trickster narrator — tenor/baritone with maximum theatrical flair, physical showmanship, and the ability to be charming and dangerous in the same breath.
avoid: Straight leading man energy — Clopin's power is unpredictability and total control over the audience's perspective

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Character voice trio — comic support for Quasimodo, each with a distinct physical and vocal personality

songs_to_prepare.title: I've Got a Little List
songs_to_prepare.why: Character voices with wit and physical expressiveness — the gargoyles are Quasi's imagination

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-gargoy.style_guidance: The gargoyles are Quasimodo's fractured inner voices — comic, loving, and ultimately revealed as projections. Each needs a distinct physical and vocal identity. Character work over vocal range.
avoid: Realistic, grounded physicality — they are stone, imagination, and comic energy

songs_to_prepare.title: Corner of the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The young man who made bad choices looking for something real — tenor regret and longing

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: A man who went out into the world and found it darker than expected — tenor self-examination

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-jehan.style_guidance: Jehan is the wayward brother — tenor with tragedy baked in. His choices explain much of Frollo's severity. Lyric quality with underlying sadness.
avoid: Villainous or cold material — Jehan is a cautionary figure, not a villain

songs_to_prepare.title: Sit Down, John
songs_to_prepare.why: Commanding baritone authority figure with historical gravity — saint as dramatic presence

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-saint-.style_guidance: Saint Aphrodisius is a supporting spiritual role — baritone with gravitas and presence. Secondary character requiring dramatic commitment within limited material.
avoid: Comic treatment — this is a solemn historical/spiritual figure

songs_to_prepare.title: My Man's Gone Now
songs_to_prepare.why: Mezzo-soprano of folk/ethnic musical heritage carrying grief and strength — Esmeralda's mother

songs_to_prepare.title: Somewhere
songs_to_prepare.why: The yearning for a safe place for your children — mezzo with tragedy and love

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-florik.style_guidance: Florika is Esmeralda's Romani mother — mezzo-soprano with folk warmth and deep tragedy. Her brief role carries enormous backstory and emotional weight.
avoid: Legit classical soprano style — Florika's voice should carry the sound of the margins, not the concert hall

songs_to_prepare.title: Make Them Hear You
songs_to_prepare.why: Principled baritone character with moral conviction — a priest who actually means it

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-father.style_guidance: Father Dupin is a supporting religious character — warm baritone who represents genuine faith rather than Frollo's weaponised version. Secondary role with moral clarity.
avoid: Dark or authoritarian material — Father Dupin is kindness, not power

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: Military baritone/tenor following orders — the man who chose institution over conscience

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-freder.style_guidance: Lieutenant Charlus is a supporting military role — baritone/tenor who serves the system. Shows how ordinary people enable extraordinary evil through compliance.
avoid: Scene-stealing material — this is a supporting role that serves the larger moral picture

songs_to_prepare.title: I've Got the Horse Right Here
songs_to_prepare.why: Speaking/character role — shows commanding presence and timing without musical demand

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-king-l.style_guidance: King Louis XI is primarily a speaking royal authority role — cast for presence, bearing, and timing. Physical majesty required.
avoid: Singing-heavy audition pieces — this is a character speaking role

songs_to_prepare.title: Hellfire (choral section)
songs_to_prepare.why: The show's choral writing is massive — four-part SATB with operatic scope

songs_to_prepare.title: Anthem
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows operatic choral capacity — this ensemble is closer to oratorio than typical musical theatre

songs_to_prepare.title: Defying Gravity
songs_to_prepare.why: Strong ensemble belt and choral blend — shows upper register capacity

hunchback-of-notre-dame/hunchback-congre.style_guidance: Hunchback requires a real SATB choir — this is not standard musical theatre ensemble. Directors should cast singers with choral training who can also act. The choral passages have near-operatic scope.
avoid: Pop-belt only ensemble — the choir writing requires genuine four-part classical choral skill

songs_to_prepare.title: No More
songs_to_prepare.why: The Baker's own defining number — baritone processing grief and responsibility with raw honesty

songs_to_prepare.title: Being Alive
songs_to_prepare.why: The everyman confronting what it means to truly connect — Sondheim in the Baker's exact register

songs_to_prepare.title: Take Me to the World
songs_to_prepare.why: Simple, aching domestic baritone — a man who wants the ordinary things that feel impossible

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the range and style — can be used as contrasting material from the same composer/show

into-the-woods/the-baker.style_guidance: The Baker is Sondheim's modern everyman — baritone with emotional intelligence and the specific quality of a good man overwhelmed by events. Conversational delivery, not operatic.
avoid: Heroic tenor material — The Baker is a baker, not a hero, and that is entirely the point

songs_to_prepare.title: Moments in the Woods
songs_to_prepare.why: The Baker's Wife's defining solo — mezzo-soprano processing a spontaneous choice with intelligence and honesty

songs_to_prepare.title: Not a Day Goes By
songs_to_prepare.why: The Sondheim mezzo soprano voice — complex, simultaneous feelings, sophisticated delivery

songs_to_prepare.title: My Favorite Things
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — warm mezzo-soprano with aspiration and a gift for subtext

songs_to_prepare.title: Losing My Mind
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the complexity of desire that co-exists with genuine love — the Baker's Wife's specific dilemma

into-the-woods/the-bakers-wife.style_guidance: The Baker's Wife is the show's most psychologically complex character — mezzo-soprano with intelligence, wit, and the ability to hold contradictions simultaneously. She is the smartest person on stage.
avoid: Simple romantic lead material — she is Sondheim's most complex woman, not a supporting wife

songs_to_prepare.title: Children Will Listen
songs_to_prepare.why: The Witch's devastating conclusion — mezzo-soprano powerhouse stripping down to cold truth

songs_to_prepare.title: Last Midnight
songs_to_prepare.why: The moment the Witch declares herself done — chilling, precise, and requires full mezzo range

songs_to_prepare.title: Rose's Turn
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who controlled through love and is left with nothing — identical energy to the Witch's arc

songs_to_prepare.title: Defying Gravity
songs_to_prepare.why: Another mezzo-soprano powerhouse who chooses not to be good — the same complex moral position

into-the-woods/the-witch.style_guidance: The Witch is the show's anchor — mezzo-soprano with genuine power to G5 combined with verbal precision. She is simultaneously right and wrong and she knows it. Never play her as a villain.
avoid: Panto witch clichés — the Witch's power is ambiguity and intelligence, not evil

songs_to_prepare.title: On the Steps of the Palace
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows Cinderella's specific voice — soprano with verbal agility, intelligence, and the famous frozen decision

songs_to_prepare.title: No One Is Alone
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the lyric warmth and emotional generosity this soprano must carry

songs_to_prepare.title: Somewhere
songs_to_prepare.why: Legit soprano yearning with genuine emotional depth

songs_to_prepare.title: I Feel Pretty
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the lighter, more comedic side — Cinderella in Act One before she has questions

into-the-woods/cinderella.style_guidance: ITW's Cinderella is the most complex version of this character — soprano who starts as a fairy tale type and becomes a thinking, questioning woman. Legit quality essential with the ability to deliver rapid Sondheim text.
avoid: Pure Disney princess soprano with no intelligence underneath — this Cinderella has agency and doubts

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: Jack's own defining number — tenor discovering a world beyond his imagination, wonder and terror

songs_to_prepare.title: Corner of the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: Young man who set out into the world and found more than he bargained for

songs_to_prepare.title: All I Need Is the Girl
songs_to_prepare.why: Young male naivety and endearing confidence — the boy who doesn't know what he doesn't know

into-the-woods/jack.style_guidance: Jack is the boy who is too young for the consequences he triggers — tenor with genuine youth, wonder, and zero comprehension of cause and effect. He is never dumb, just incomplete.
avoid: Calculating or knowing performance — Jack's tragedy is that he acts from pure feeling, every time

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know Things Now
songs_to_prepare.why: Little Red's post-wolf education — soprano/belt showing the character's dawning awareness

songs_to_prepare.title: Not While I'm Around
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — shows the innocent child's fierce protective instinct, different tone from the comic scenes

songs_to_prepare.title: Wouldn't It Be Loverly
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows the young soprano with appetite and pragmatism — Little Red BEFORE the woods

into-the-woods/little-red-riding-hood.style_guidance: Little Red is the show's most rapidly maturing character — bright soprano with physical energy and the ability to go from oblivious to knowing within a scene. Comic and then chilling.
avoid: Sweet, innocent-only performance — Little Red's whole arc is the loss of innocent obliviousness

songs_to_prepare.title: Agony
songs_to_prepare.why: The Prince's own comic duet — everything about this character in two-and-a-half minutes of glorious self-obsession

songs_to_prepare.title: Willkommen
songs_to_prepare.why: Seductive baritone who is entirely aware of his own effect — glamour without depth

songs_to_prepare.title: Some Enchanted Evening
songs_to_prepare.why: Romantic baritone who falls completely for the fantasy — then proves entirely unable to live up to it

into-the-woods/cinderellas-prince.style_guidance: The Princes are the show's great comic deconstruction of romantic heroes — handsome, useless, completely sincere about their own suffering. Play it absolutely straight. The comedy comes from total earnestness.
avoid: Knowing winks about the comedy — any self-awareness kills the joke. These princes are perfectly serious.

songs_to_prepare.title: Agony
songs_to_prepare.why: Both Princes share this comic masterpiece — identical guidance to Cinderella's Prince

songs_to_prepare.title: The Impossible Dream
songs_to_prepare.why: Delusional romantic conviction delivered with complete sincerity — the Prince believes every word

into-the-woods/rapunzels-prince.style_guidance: Same as Cinderella's Prince — comic romantic hero who is absolutely convinced of his own anguished nobility. The earnestness IS the performance. Baritone with range and complete self-belief.
avoid: Ironic performance — if either Prince seems to know they are funny, the show loses one of its best gags

songs_to_prepare.title: In My Own Little Corner
songs_to_prepare.why: Pure soprano dreaming from isolation — the precise emotional reality of a girl in a tower

songs_to_prepare.title: Castle on a Cloud
songs_to_prepare.why: The lonely child's dream of warmth and freedom — Rapunzel pre-wedding, all longing

songs_to_prepare.title: Glitter and Be Gay
songs_to_prepare.why: If a more comic approach — shows soprano range and the brittle brightness of someone trying to adapt

into-the-woods/rapunzel.style_guidance: Rapunzel is a pure lyric soprano — she goes mad quietly, which is one of the show's darkest moments. The contrast between her ethereal beauty and her fragmentation must be present from the start.
avoid: Belty or contemporary pop approach — Rapunzel is pure legit soprano, specifically chosen to contrast with the Witch

songs_to_prepare.title: Rose's Turn
songs_to_prepare.why: The mother at the end of her rope, loving and maddened — soprano/mezzo with exasperation and genuine fear

songs_to_prepare.title: Far From the Home I Love
songs_to_prepare.why: A mother facing terrible choices to protect her child — warmth, grief, and pragmatism

into-the-woods/jacks-mother.style_guidance: Jack's Mother is poverty, love, and frustration in one package — soprano/mezzo with roughness under the warmth. She is managing disaster with dignity.
avoid: Gentle, refined soprano — Jack's Mother is poor, harried, and running out of options

songs_to_prepare.title: Old Friends
songs_to_prepare.why: A Sondheim baritone who carries the story's weight — observational, warm, slightly complicit

songs_to_prepare.title: The Road You Didn't Take
songs_to_prepare.why: The man watching other people's stories with full knowledge of outcome — the Mysterious Man in song form

into-the-woods/narrator-mysterious-man.style_guidance: The Narrator/Mysterious Man is the show's meta-theatrical conscience — warm baritone with intelligence and slight sadness. He knows more than the characters and eventually must enter the story.
avoid: Detached or cold performance — the Narrator loves these characters even as he chronicles their mistakes

songs_to_prepare.title: Everything's Coming Up Roses
songs_to_prepare.why: The mother who will sacrifice everything — including her children's health — for social ambition

songs_to_prepare.title: I'm Still Here
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who clawed her way to respectability and will die before she lets anyone take it — mezzo with teeth

into-the-woods/cinderellas-stepmother.style_guidance: The Stepmother is social climbing with a beautiful veneer and vicious core — mezzo-soprano with sharp delivery and a smile that doesn't reach the eyes. She is the show's comic villain.
avoid: Broad cackling villain — the Stepmother thinks she is being entirely reasonable and that is far funnier

songs_to_prepare.title: Popular
songs_to_prepare.why: The girl who is convinced her mediocrity is excellence — mezzo with comedy and total self-belief

songs_to_prepare.title: I Enjoy Being a Girl
songs_to_prepare.why: Mezzo character who is thoroughly pleased with herself — charming, slightly dim, absolutely confident

into-the-woods/florinda.style_guidance: Florinda is the stepsister who literally cuts off her heel to fit the slipper — mezzo with physical comedy and absolute conviction of her own worthiness. She and Lucinda are a double act.
avoid: Knowing self-deprecation — the stepsisters are completely sincere in their delusion

songs_to_prepare.title: Popular
songs_to_prepare.why: Same stepsister energy as Florinda — complete conviction of superiority

songs_to_prepare.title: Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend
songs_to_prepare.why: Mezzo character who is thoroughly invested in social status and completely sure of her own charm

into-the-woods/lucinda.style_guidance: Mirror image of Florinda — mezzo with the same combination of physical comedy, total self-belief, and complete obliviousness. The stepsisters should feel like an act.
avoid: Malicious reading — the stepsisters aren't evil, they're just spectacular idiots

songs_to_prepare.title: Hello, Young Lovers
songs_to_prepare.why: Seductive baritone who watches the young with predatory warmth — exactly The Wolf's register

songs_to_prepare.title: The Music of the Night
songs_to_prepare.why: Dark seduction — the powerful figure drawing in the innocent with honeyed voice

into-the-woods/the-wolf.style_guidance: The Wolf is sexual menace in a top hat — baritone with pure seductive danger. The role is deliberately uncomfortable and that discomfort is the theatrical point. Lush voice, predatory physicality.
avoid: Comic reading — The Wolf is genuinely threatening beneath the theatrical glamour

songs_to_prepare.title: Not While I'm Around
songs_to_prepare.why: The spirit of pure protective motherhood from the grave — lyric soprano with warmth and gentle authority

songs_to_prepare.title: Climb Ev'ry Mountain
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano with spiritual authority — gentle, elevated, and guiding from a safe remove

into-the-woods/cinderellas-mother.style_guidance: Cinderella's Mother is a pure lyric soprano spirit — ethereal, warm, and guiding. A small role with enormous impact when cast with a genuinely beautiful pure soprano tone.
avoid: Belt or character approach — Cinderella's Mother should float above the story, not anchor it

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: The official functionary who represents institutional order — character presenter role

into-the-woods/the-steward.style_guidance: The Steward is a small ensemble/character speaking role — cast for physical presence and timing. He represents the royal hierarchy at work.
avoid: Large vocal showcase — this is a supporting character role

songs_to_prepare.title: Physical Theatre Demonstration
songs_to_prepare.why: Milky White is a non-speaking physical role — show physical mime, relationship dynamics, and character commitment

into-the-woods/milky-white.style_guidance: Milky White is a pure physical theatre role — cast entirely on movement, comic timing, and the ability to form a convincing and endearing cow-actor relationship with Jack. Some productions give Milky White a spoken or sung moment.
avoid: Vocal audition showcase — this role is entirely about physical performance and character puppetry

songs_to_prepare.title: Some Things Are Meant to Be
songs_to_prepare.why: Shows a large, powerful voice that can convey both grief and terrifying authority — the Giant's wife is mourning

into-the-woods/the-giant.style_guidance: The Giant is an amplified voice-only or enormous physical role — requires a voice that fills every corner of the theatre with both terror and grief. She is not a monster; she is bereaved.
avoid: Roaring, cartoon monster approach — the Giant's Wife is grieving, not malicious
